```{python}
ba = aa.before_after(ph)
c, r, t = ba.iloc[0], ba.iloc[1], ba.iloc[2]
labels = ["Click rate", "Report rate"]
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=labels, y=[c["pre_rate"], r["pre_rate"]], name=f"Before push ({c['pre_window']})", marker_color=ap.MUTED,
                     error_y=dict(type="data", symmetric=False, array=[c["pre_high"] - c["pre_rate"], r["pre_high"] - r["pre_rate"]],
                                  arrayminus=[c["pre_rate"] - c["pre_low"], r["pre_rate"] - r["pre_low"]], color=ap._rgba(ap.TEXT, 0.45), thickness=1.5, width=4),
                     text=[pct(c["pre_rate"]), pct(r["pre_rate"])], textposition="outside", textfont=dict(size=14),
                     hovertemplate="%{x}<br>before %{y:.1%}<extra></extra>"))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=labels, y=[c["post_rate"], r["post_rate"]], name=f"After push ({c['post_window']})",
                     marker_color=[ap.CLICK, ap.REPORT],
                     error_y=dict(type="data", symmetric=False, array=[c["post_high"] - c["post_rate"], r["post_high"] - r["post_rate"]],
                                  arrayminus=[c["post_rate"] - c["post_low"], r["post_rate"] - r["post_low"]], color=ap._rgba(ap.TEXT, 0.45), thickness=1.5, width=4),
                     text=[pct(c["post_rate"]), pct(r["post_rate"])], textposition="outside", textfont=dict(size=14),
                     hovertemplate="%{x}<br>after %{y:.1%}<extra></extra>"))
ap.base_layout(fig, f"After the training push, clicks fell {100*(1-c['post_rate']/c['pre_rate']):.0f}% and reports rose {100*(r['post_rate']/r['pre_rate']-1):.0f}%",
               "Six months before versus six months after the March 2026 Phishing Defense launch (March excluded as the rollout month), 95% CI",
               ytitle="Share of delivered emails", height=460)
fig.update_layout(barmode="group", hovermode="x unified", bargap=0.3)
show(fig)
```

### Column {width=45%}

```{python}
#| title: "Before/after, adjusted for template difficulty, department and role"
txt = f"""
<div class="finding">
<p>Because later campaigns used harder templates, the raw before/after comparison <i>understates</i> the improvement. A logistic regression with a before/after indicator plus template difficulty, department and role (standard errors clustered by person) gives:</p>
<ul>
<li><b>Clicking:</b> odds ratio <b>{c['adjusted_odds_ratio']:.2f}</b> (95% CI {c['or_low']:.2f} to {c['or_high']:.2f}). The odds of a click after the push are about {100*(1-c['adjusted_odds_ratio']):.0f}% lower than before, for the same template difficulty.</li>
<li><b>Reporting:</b> odds ratio <b>{r['adjusted_odds_ratio']:.2f}</b> (95% CI {r['or_low']:.2f} to {r['or_high']:.2f}).</li>
<li><b>Time to first report:</b> median {t['pre_rate']:.0f} minutes before (95% CI {t['pre_low']:.0f} to {t['pre_high']:.0f}) versus <b>{t['post_rate']:.0f} minutes</b> after (95% CI {t['post_low']:.0f} to {t['post_high']:.0f}).</li>
</ul>
<p>The "before" window includes the October Awareness Month bump, which makes this a conservative comparison. This is an observational before/after design: it shows the program improved, not that training alone caused every point of the change. The difference-in-differences analysis below isolates the training itself.</p>
</div>
"""
display(HTML(txt))
```

```{python}
did = aa.training_did(ph, tr)
eff = did["effects"].set_index("metric")
cells = did["cells"]
cc = cells[cells["metric"] == "click_rate"]
fig = go.Figure()
for period, color in (("Before push", ap.MUTED), ("After push", ap.CLICK)):
    s = cc[cc["period"] == period].set_index("group").loc[["Not completed", "Completed by due date"]].reset_index()
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(x=s["group"], y=s["rate"], name=period, marker_color=color,
                         error_y=dict(type="data", symmetric=False, array=s["ci_high"] - s["rate"], arrayminus=s["rate"] - s["ci_low"],
                                      color=ap._rgba(ap.TEXT, 0.45), thickness=1.5, width=4),
                         text=[pct(v) for v in s["rate"]], textposition="outside", textfont=dict(size=14),
                         hovertemplate="%{x}<br>" + period + " %{y:.1%}<extra></extra>"))
e = eff.loc["click_rate"]
ap.base_layout(fig, f"Training completion predicts lower clicking: difference-in-differences odds ratio {e['did_odds_ratio']:.2f} (95% CI {e['or_low']:.2f} to {e['or_high']:.2f})",
               f"Click rate before (Sep 2025 to Feb 2026) and after (May to Sep 2026) by training status. {did['excluded_late']:,} late completers excluded.",
               ytitle="Click rate", height=470)
fig.update_layout(barmode="group", hovermode="x unified", bargap=0.3)
show(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: "Does training completion predict lower click rate?"
er = eff.loc["report_rate"]
cr = cells[cells["metric"] == "report_rate"].set_index(["group", "period"])["rate"]
sc = did["status_counts"].set_index("status")["people"]
txt = f"""
<div class="finding">
<p><b>Yes, and the estimate survives a stricter test than a simple comparison.</b> People who complete training are probably more security-minded to begin with, so comparing completers with non-completers after the push would flatter the training. The difference-in-differences design compares each group with <i>its own</i> pre-push baseline:</p>
<ul>
<li><b>Click rate:</b> completers went from {pct(cells.query("metric=='click_rate' and group=='Completed by due date' and period=='Before push'")['rate'].iloc[0])} to {pct(cells.query("metric=='click_rate' and group=='Completed by due date' and period=='After push'")['rate'].iloc[0])}; non-completers from {pct(cells.query("metric=='click_rate' and group=='Not completed' and period=='Before push'")['rate'].iloc[0])} to {pct(cells.query("metric=='click_rate' and group=='Not completed' and period=='After push'")['rate'].iloc[0])}. Adjusted interaction odds ratio <b>{e['did_odds_ratio']:.2f}</b> (95% CI {e['or_low']:.2f} to {e['or_high']:.2f}).</li>
<li><b>Report rate:</b> completers {pct(cr[('Completed by due date','Before push')])} to {pct(cr[('Completed by due date','After push')])}; non-completers {pct(cr[('Not completed','Before push')])} to {pct(cr[('Not completed','After push')])}. Interaction odds ratio <b>{er['did_odds_ratio']:.2f}</b> (95% CI {er['or_low']:.2f} to {er['or_high']:.2f}).</li>
</ul>
<p>Groups: {sc['Completed by due date']:,} completed by the due date, {sc['Not completed']:,} had not completed by the end of the period, and {sc['Completed late']:,} late completers were set aside so the "after" window is clean. Non-completers also improved a little, consistent with newsletters and the general awareness push reaching everyone.</p>
</div>
"""
display(HTML(txt))
```

## Row

```{python}
#| title: "How to read this page"
display(HTML("""
<div class="finding">
<ul>
<li><b>Before/after</b> answers "did things improve?" It is the simplest view and the one leadership asks for first.</li>
<li><b>Repeat clickers</b> are the people most likely to cause an incident. A falling count means the program is reaching the right people, not just raising the average.</li>
<li><b>Difference-in-differences</b> answers "did <i>training</i> do it?" by removing the part of the improvement that non-completers also experienced.</li>
<li><b>Event attendance</b> is reported descriptively because attendance was voluntary; a causal claim would need a randomised invitation design.</li>
<li>All estimates use 95% confidence intervals; standard errors in the regression models are clustered by person because each person is tested 18 times.</li>
</ul>
</div>
"""))
```
